title: S4 invalidation volume (Agent 5, task #20): one functional devoff2 run with slow_frame_log_ms=1 (logging only, not for timing)
notes: Purpose: per-frame CPU-side invalidation volume on the devoff GPU path, for S4 (perf-notes/agent5-uploads.md, S4 section). slow_frame_log_ms=1 makes the existing ReportSlowFrame (rexglue-sdk src/graphics/d3d12/command_processor.cpp:242-283, called once per swap at :2193) log every frame. Its 'cpu-write invalidations Nx K KB' is the count and requested bytes of every PhysicalHeap::TriggerCallbacks call that hit a GPU-watched page: the game's MmSetAddressProtect (PhysicalHeap::Protect, xmemory.cpp:2132-2136), CPU write faults, file reads, alloc/free. It is a volume and an upper bound for the re-upload. It cannot show whether the re-uploaded bytes changed; no existing counter can.

Same bin, phase and window as a-prof in build/agent8/matrix/20261122-0357: devoff2-bin, framerate_limit=0, title/attract loop, 10 s settle + 60 s warm-up after the first frame, 150 s window. The volume then lines up with that profile's 3.6 ms/f upload cost. No profiler, no input.

Analysis: python bench/agent5/s4_slowframe.py <run dir> (window 70-220 s after the first logged frame, the a-prof window) prints the per-frame count and KB distribution and MB/s. Logging every frame costs a little time, so this run is functional only, never timing.
Checks (Agent 8): status OK, clean WM_CLOSE, about one 'slow frame #' line per frame (the script reports index gaps), [error] count no higher than a-prof (0).

arms.note: devoff2 + slow_frame_log_ms=1 (logging only), uncapped like a-prof; functional, not for timing
